We seek clinically excellent mission-driven physicians at all levels of experience who thrive in an academic safety-net environment and are eager to contribute to scholarship, teaching, and health system improvement while delivering outstanding care to our patient population. ZSFG serves as San Francisco’s safety-net hospital, providing care to patients with complex medical, social, and structural challenges. Position description The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management (ESPM) at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor nine-month faculty position in the area of Arthropod Biodiversity. Biodiversity lies at the heart of all ecosystems, from the smallest microbiomes to the global expanses of continents, oceans, and the atmosphere. It holds intrinsic value across many dimensions, encompassing species, genes, functions, processes, and cultures, while also providing tangible benefits such as food, medicine, and other natural products. Biodiversity underpins essential ecosystem services, including clean air, water, and soil, and contributes profoundly to human health, cultural identity, and psychological well-being. Arthropods, which E.O. Wilson famously described as “the little things that run the world,” are the majority of Earth’s macrobiota and have recently faced threats from multiple stressors, including climate change, habitat loss and degradation, and cumulative use of agricultural chemicals. Loss of biodiversity, both locally (α-diversity) and among locations (β-diversity) is occurring at a rate exceeding our current efforts to discover, document, and understand the species with which we share our planet. These patterns are particularly true for arthropods, with insects showing global declines in populations across multiple orders (sometimes referred to as “insect apocalypse”). At the species level, arthropods now represent 70-80% of the documented loss of biodiversity. At the same time, many other arthropods are becoming increasingly problematic as invasive species, pests of agriculture and forests, and vectors of plant and animal pathogens. Expertise is needed in understanding drivers of arthropod biodiversity change, including understanding processes leading to resilient populations, communities, and ecosystems. ESPM is a multidisciplinary community of scholars from across the sciences and humanities who conduct research, teaching, and outreach to advance scientific understanding and develop solutions for the world’s pressing environmental problems. ESPM is home to a top-ranked Ph.D. program in environmental science, environmental studies, and ecological/evolutionary biology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department. ESPM is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. Position description The Department of Architecture at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Computation and Design Methods. Berkeley's Department of Architecture sits within the College of Environmental Design, a leader in cross-disciplinary environmental design education since 1959, and is uniquely positioned in the Bay Area, where design practice, technological innovation, and critical inquiry converge in uncommon proximity; for more information, visit UC Berkeley's Department of Architecture. We seek candidates whose work examines and/or demonstrates promise in applying computation as a creative, social, and technical force in architectural design, connecting systems, tools, and intelligent environments to questions of authorship, agency, governance, participation, and the changing responsibilities of design. "Computation and Design Methods" names a broad area of inquiry concerned with how tools, systems, data, media, and methods shape architectural design, representation, research, and practice. Its primary concern is the study and making of socio-technical systems through which design activity is organized, coordinated, and governed, and design artifacts are generated, represented, and evaluated. Possible areas of focus include technically-oriented subjects such as building information modeling, digital twins, spatial data systems, and urban information systems; methodological inquiry such as feedback systems, human-building interaction, participation, distributed agency, and self-regulating processes; and sociotechnical and critical research such as platform studies, civic data, public-interest technology, and built-environment science and technology studies. Across these areas, the field asks how computation operates in architectural design as means, as material, and as media, ultimately shaping how the built environment is experienced and inhabited over time. That is: as a way of making and evaluating design work, as a technical substrate shaped and incorporated into designed artifacts, and as a system that acts back on design practice and culture. This search responds to a moment in which computation is rapidly reshaping design knowledge, pedagogy, and practice. As data-rich, automated, and intelligent systems transform how buildings are conceived, coordinated, evaluated, and inhabited, the need for critical frameworks has never been more pressing. Artificial intelligence, as much a cultural force as a technical one, has generated expectations, anxieties, and professional reorganizations that now bear directly on how architecture is taught, practiced, and understood. The College of Environmental Design’s foundational work on “wicked problems,” feedback, participation, patterns, and design-as-argumentation offers an urgently needed foundation for preparing designers to act responsibly within this transformed landscape, recognizing that technical decisions are inseparable from their human, social, and environmental consequences. Position description The Department of Film & Media at the University of California, Berkeley seeks applications for an Assistant Professor (tenure track) in the area of Critical/Experimental Film and Video Production. The Department of Film and Media at the University of California, Berkeley is one of the oldest film programs in the United States with a strong foundation in national and transnational film histories and theories and growing interest in a wide range of media practices, industries, and cultures. The Department holds a strong intellectual commitment to innovative interdisciplinary approaches to film and media research, evidenced in the scholarship of its thirteen current ladder faculty, five of whom have officially shared appointments with other departments in the Division of Arts & Humanities. Position description The Goldman School of Public Policy at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for a tenure-track appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank in the area of policy analysis and/or governmental management and public administration. Against the backdrop of a world with fractured institutional trust, increased social stratification and inequality, diverse populations, dispersed decision-making, media and informational fragmentation, political and governmental volatility, skepticism about evidence, and the growing use of AI, the Goldman School seeks a faculty member whose research considers the changing role of public policy analysis and/or the changing nature of governmental management. The Goldman School encourages applications from scholars in a broad range of disciplines, including public policy, political science, economics, public affairs, sociology, psychology, business, and law, as well as data scientists with roots in computer science, schools of information, economics, and other fields, whose research engages with questions of public policy and/or public administration. We welcome applications from researchers studying these topics in the United States and around the world. The successful candidate will advance innovative, data-driven approaches to public policy and administration by integrating behavioral science and analytics into both research and teaching; develop and deliver rigorous courses that enhance student competencies in policy analysis, public sector management, organizational behavior, and evidence-based policymaking; collaborate with a diverse faculty to support interdisciplinary research and reinforce the School’s broader public policy mission; and apply cutting-edge scholarly insights to pressing social problems by producing research that meaningfully informs and improves public policy and government performance. Position description The School of Information at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank. Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a field of expertise focused on the evolving relationship between people and computing systems. HCI researchers design and study new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with technology, and investigate how emerging computing systems shape human capabilities, practices, organizations, and society. Methods include the design and development of novel systems, experimentation, qualitative and ethnographic research, participatory design, computational methods, field studies, and mixed-methods research. We seek applicants who are defining the next generation of human-computer interaction: developing new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with increasingly intelligent computing systems. We are particularly interested in scholars who both imagine and build new forms of human-computer interaction and rigorously investigate how these technologies shape people, organizations, and society. We welcome research across HCI and related fields, including, but not limited to, human-AI interaction and collaboration, intelligent and adaptive interfaces, social and collaborative computing, the future of work, accessibility, values such as sustainability, privacy, and justice in and through design, ubiquitous and embodied computing, information visualization, human-robot interaction, and emerging interaction modalities. We welcome a broad range of methodological approaches, including the design and development of novel systems, experimental and computational methods, qualitative and ethnographic research, field studies, participatory and critical design methods, and mixed-methods approaches. Successful candidates will demonstrate the potential to establish an internationally recognized research program, contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in HCI, and engage with the School of Information’s interdisciplinary community. The School of Information is a graduate research and education community committed to expanding access to information and to improving its usability, reliability, and credibility while preserving security and privacy. Position description The Department of Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning (LAEP) at UC Berkeley seeks to fill a tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to contemporary design discourse on “Landscape and Eco-Technology” through disciplinary engagement, teaching, research and/or practice. This position will allow the department to carry forward its legacy of leadership in service of the State of California, the nation, and the wider world. It also will further the department’s disciplinary knowledge on public infrastructure through teaching, design, and/or research in material, vegetal, topographical, and hydrologic landscape systems. We seek a colleague whose approach encompasses cultural meaning and critical discourse as well as performance-based assessment and design engagement. The Department of Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning at UC Berkeley is California’s flagship program. As an accredited professional program in an R1 institution, the department expects its faculty to carry out research and/or creative practice that is recognized nationally and internationally and to support pedagogy that critically advances the role of Eco-Technology in contemporary design, praxis, and landscape performance. Landscape architecture has a long and distinguished history at Berkeley, starting in 1913 and boasting a renowned cast of alumni and faculty. Today, we offer degree programs at the undergraduate, Masters, and PhD levels. As one of the founding departments in the College of Environmental Design, established in 1959, interdisciplinarity is part of our ethos and public engagement of our mission. Building on the legacy of environmental design, we tackle contemporary challenges from climate adaptation to societal crises across methods, technologies, and media (UC Berkeley’s Department of Landscape Architecture & Environmental Planning). Landscape and Eco-Technology is integral to the resilience, performance, and equity of urban systems. By considering scales and typologies—from site-based construction practices to national climate adaptation strategies, circularity, and carbon policy—we can establish partnerships and enrich disciplinary discourse. Eco-Technology comes into play across topographic, hydrologic, vegetated, and material systems that define contemporary landscape architectural praxis. It requires a synthetic understanding of how landscape systems are connected and are comprehensively designed, modeled, and prototyped. Our department recognizes Eco-Technology as a core competency within landscape architecture, one that is indispensable to the creation of livable, inclusive, and healthy sustainable cities. The successful candidate will help develop courses in the area of Eco-Technology as well as contribute to the department and beyond through collaboration and mentoring. We recognize that scholarship in landscape architecture encompasses research, applied research, and creative practice. Position description The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology in the Rausser College of Natural Resources at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor faculty position in “Plant Responses to Environmental Changes”. The department is a community of scholars whose research advances knowledge in plant and microbial systems in terms of biochemistry, cell and developmental biology, genetics and genomics, ecology, evolution, and pathogenesis, and their applications to ecosystems, agriculture, bioenergy, biomedicine, and biotechnology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department, and we administer top-ranked Ph.D. programs in microbiology and plant biology. Our researchers benefit from having access to extensive greenhouse and field space and opportunities for interactions and collaborations with other biological science departments and units on campus, including the Innovative Genomics Institute, the Energy Biosciences Institute, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and the Food Institute, as well as additional local research centers, including the Plant Gene Expression Center, the Joint Genomics Institute, and the Joint Bioenergy Institute. The department seeks applicants conducting fundamental research to provide knowledge on how plants respond and adapt to environmental changes, including abiotic stress factors (e.g., temperature, drought, flooding, salinity) and biotic interactions (e.g., pathogenic and symbiotic microbial interactions, insects, parasitic plants, etc.). The candidate’s research will be expected to integrate a broad spectrum of cutting-edge genetic, genomic, physiological, quantitative analysis and modeling, systems biology, and/or synthetic biology approaches. Applicants should also have strong interests in teaching and mentoring the next generation of scientists in plant biology. Candidates whose research programs include both fundamental biology and translational research bearing on crop improvement, particularly in the context of adaptation to climate change-associated environmental challenges, are especially encouraged to apply. The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology recognizes the intrinsic relationship between diversity and excellence in all our endeavors; we embrace open and equitable access to opportunities for learning and development of all members as our obligation and goal. The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non-traditional career paths or who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website. Position description The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of California, Berkeley, invites tenure-track faculty applications in Sustainable Energy Infrastructure. Preference will be given to candidates who are recent Ph.D. graduates, postdocs or Assistant Professors. About the Position: As demands for energy grow and corresponding environmental impacts intensify, the need for sustainable, transformative, resilient, and financially affordable solutions in energy infrastructure has never been greater. Energy infrastructure lies at the nexus of civil engineering, environmental stewardship, affordability, and societal progress. It includes clean and affordable approaches to energy integration, generation, and storage; management of emissions and wastes; geo-energy and geological systems; food-energy-water systems; and the design of new and modernization of existing infrastructure to meet energy demands sustainably. The related challenges are multifaceted throughout the life cycles of energy infrastructure—requiring expertise in materials, emissions and impact assessment, environmental impact mitigation, systems analysis, and resiliency to hazards and climate extremes. Multidisciplinary research interests are expected. The Department’s leadership in research, education, and professional engagement positions it to cultivate groundbreaking advances that will redefine energy infrastructure and its interactions with society for the 21st century. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape the future and contribute to a cleaner, healthier, cost-efficient, and resilient world. We seek a visionary scholar who will lead research in new directions in energy systems, foster partnerships with industry and government, and educate the next generation of engineers to lead this transformation. Such efforts will lead to cross-cutting research and collaboration in any area of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Faculty are expected to be leaders in research, contribute to existing undergraduate and graduate educational programs in the Department, and develop new and innovative courses. New hires are also expected to collaborate with colleagues in the Department, the College of Engineering, and more broadly on the Berkeley Campus. About the Department: Our faculty are leaders in research, establishing new fields of study and developing advanced models and tools to address critical societal-scale challenges. We prepare students for leadership roles in industry, academia, and the public sector, empowering them to shape a sustainable future. We provide technical expertise, leadership, and service to public, private, and professional entities worldwide. Position description The Department of Plant and Microbial Biology in the Rausser College of Natural Resources at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor faculty position in "Plant- or Macroalgae-Associated Microbial Communities and Interactions." The department is a community of scholars whose research advances knowledge in plant and microbial systems in terms of biochemistry, cell and developmental biology, genetics and genomics, ecology, evolution, and pathogenesis, and their applications to ecosystems, agriculture, bioenergy, biomedicine, and biotechnology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department, and we administer top-ranked Ph.D. programs in microbiology and plant biology. Our researchers benefit from having access to extensive greenhouse and field space and opportunities for interactions and collaborations with other biological science departments and units on campus. This position centers on research into how plants or macroalgae and their associated microbial communities jointly respond and adapt to environmental stressors, contributing to climate-resilient crops and microbial systems. The scope of the position spans, but is not limited to: plant-microbiome or macroalgae-microbiome interactions in the context of pathogen defense (viral, bacterial, or fungal disease); soil microbial communities and their role in reducing agricultural dependence on pesticides, fertilizers, and greenhouse gas emissions; and microbial associations with macroalgae relevant to cultivation, health, and climate resilience in the emerging bioeconomy. Research in this position will complement and build on existing strengths in PMB, with opportunities for collaboration through our existing partnerships, e.g. the Innovative Genomics Institute, the Energy & Biosciences Institute, the International Bioeconomy & Macroalgae Center, the Plant Gene Expression Center, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, the Berkeley Food Institute, the Joint Genomics Institute, and the Joint Bioenergy Institute, and other campus and national lab partners. These partnerships support research that integrates fundamental discovery with translational applications for agricultural and environmental resilience. The faculty member appointed to this position will teach and mentor the next generation of scientists in plant and microbial biology, including contributing to PMB's growing undergraduate and graduate curricula in this area. Position description The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE), at the University of California, San Diego, invites applications for an Assistant Professor position in Fusion Energy Engineering. We seek exceptional candidates with research interests in fusion engineering including, but not limited to: 1) Engineering of fusion energy components and systems, with particular emphasis on thermal management and thermo-fluid phenomena, and with consideration of related MAE disciplines. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: management of high heat and neutron fluxes on first-wall and divertor systems; tritium-breeding blankets, including neutron transport, shielding, activation, and radiation damage; and thermo-fluid engineering of liquid-metal and molten-salt systems. 2) Fusion power plant systems engineering and integration. The activities of the newly appointed Assistant Professor will be synergistic with those of existing Department faculty working in fusion plasma physics, laser-plasma interactions and pulsed power, plasma-material interactions, thermofluids, photonics, materials in extreme conditions, mechanics of materials, and other related areas. Exceptional candidates without a background in fusion energy, but with strong expertise in one or more of the areas identified above, are strongly encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will be expected to build upon their existing expertise to develop an independent and internationally recognized research program that contributes to the advancement of fusion energy science and technology at UC San Diego. Position description The Department of Plant Pathology in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Plant Pathology with an emphasis on plant health and microbiomes. This is an academic year (9-month), tenure-track Assistant Professor position that includes an appointment in the California Agricultural Experiment Station (AES), with responsibility for research and outreach relevant to the AES mission, as well as university service. The appointee is expected to establish a competitive, externally funded research program in plant microbiome science that addresses critical and emerging issues in plant pathology. The program should advance microbiome-informed approaches to the diagnosis, prediction, and/or management of plant diseases and develop science-based solutions to promote plant health. Research should generate fundamental and applied understanding of the composition, function, and/or dynamics of plant-associated microbial communities (including bacteria, fungi, oomycetes, viruses, and/or other microorganisms) and their interactions with plant hosts and each other. Areas of interest may include disease-suppressive microbiomes, dysbiosis and pathobiomes, host-microbiome-pathogen interactions, pathogen-pathogen and pathogen-nonpathogen interactions, disease complexes and multi-infections, microbiome engineering, synthetic communities, and the ecology and evolution of pathogens within the phytomicrobiome. Research may also address climate-driven changes in plant-microbiome interactions and emerging diseases, span model, agricultural, and/or natural plant systems, and should have a strong mechanistic and/or predictive foundation. The appointee will complement existing departmental strengths in plant-microbe interactions, disease epidemiology, and disease management, while expanding microbiome-informed approaches relevant to food security, agricultural sustainability, climate resilience, and the broader One Health framework. The appointee will be expected to teach GDB103: The Microbiome of People, Animals and Plants, a 3-unit, upper-division undergraduate course that serves Global Disease Biology (GDB) and other students. The appointee is also expected to contribute to required GDB courses, such as GDB90: Introduction to Global Disease Biology, GDB 187: Global Disease Biology Seminar, and PMI129Y: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces, and will have opportunities to contribute to graduate courses such as PLP201B: Ecology and Epidemiology of Plant Pathogenic Organisms and PLP298: Microbial Ecology. Training and mentoring of graduate students, undergraduate student advising, curricular development, outreach, and departmental and university service are expected. The successful candidate will be an active member of the Plant Pathology Graduate Program and other graduate groups as appropriate and will have opportunities to collaborate with Cooperative Extension specialists and advisors, relevant industries, and other public stakeholders. This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant Professor rank, and the resulting appointment will be at that rank regardless of the appointee's qualifications.

We are particularly interested in candidates studying stress, resilience, and health; social and emotional influences on health; psychophysiological or biopsychosocial pathways; health behavior and behavior change; psychological contributors to health disparities; and/or interventions designed to improve health and well-being. Although candidates may draw upon social, clinical, developmental, affective, or neuroscience perspectives, the position is intended to strengthen the department’s core research and teaching capacity in health psychology. The successful candidate will be expected to teach foundational undergraduate and graduate courses in health psychology, contribute additional courses in their area of expertise, mentor students, and maintain an active program of research with strong potential for external funding. The Department of Psychology values collaborative and interdisciplinary scholarship. Faculty have opportunities to collaborate across the School of Social Ecology and with researchers throughout UC Irvine, including those in public health, medicine, nursing, biological sciences, and related fields and centers (e.g., the Center for Biomarker & Biobehavioral Research). The successful candidate would join the faculty of the Music Department as an Assistant Teaching Professor, and would join the core faculty of UCSC’s Creative Technologies program, a multi-departmental, online undergraduate major whose faculty are dedicated to advanced, innovative web-based arts and design pedagogy, and a curriculum that cultivates imagination, justice, and empowered community in digital contexts. Assistant Professors of Teaching are members of the Academic Senate. The Teaching Professor series includes eligibility for review for promotion to Associate Professor of Teaching, which includes security of employment (equivalent to tenure). The primary duties and responsibilities of an appointee to the position are pedagogical (e.g. teaching, and advising). In addition, the hire will provide quantitative support to students, postdocs, and faculty through a pre-defined number of weekly consulting hours (akin to office hours), and will offer 1-2 seminars each year to help department faculty stay up to date on emerging quantitative and computational methods. We seek a colleague who will deepen Berkeley's leadership in housing research and help shape its future direction. The POMDC at UCSD is committed to the tripartite academic mission of excellence in clinical care, teaching, and research. Position description The Department of Psychology and the Department of Urban Planning and Public Policy (UPPP) in the School of Social Ecology at the University of California, Irvine, invite applications for a joint tenure-track faculty position at the Associate Professor level in Behavior Change, Decision Science, and Policy. The position will advance research on how individuals and groups make decisions, change behavior, and respond to interventions, institutions, and public policy. We seek scholars who connect behavioral science to important real-world problems with a strong commitment to translating research into effective interventions, actionable programs, and policy solutions. The successful candidate will complement the Department of Psychology’s strengths in basic and applied behavioral research (spanning developmental, health, social, or clinical domains) as well as UPPP’s focus on public policy, inequality, social problems and environmental issues. Interdisciplinary Research and Policy We welcome scholars whose research examines behavior change and decision-making––such as motivation, beliefs, social influence, self-regulation, and risk perception––and connects them to policy design, practice, and broader societal outcomes. We are particularly interested in candidates who bridge individual-level psychological science with social, institutional, community, or environmental contexts. The successful candidate will advance an interdisciplinary agenda that explores both how policy shapes human behavior and how behavioral insights can optimize the design, evaluation, and translation of public interventions and policies. This joint appointment offers rich opportunities for collaboration across Psychology, Urban Planning and Public Policy, the School of Social Ecology, and the broader UC Irvine campus. Teaching and Mentoring The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in Psychology and UPPP. Teaching may include courses addressing behavior change, decision-making, behavioral science, public policy, urban planning, and/or the candidate's substantive area of expertise. The candidate will mentor students across disciplinary boundaries and contribute to preparing students to apply psychological and behavioral science to complex social and policy problems. Qualifications Candidates must have a doctoral degree in psychology, public policy, urban planning, or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Position description The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Associate/Full Professor of Agricultural Economics. This is an academic year (9-month), tenured Associate/Full Professor position with a 20% Instruction and Research (I&R), and 80% Agricultural Experiment Station (AES) appointment. The appointee is expected to establish an outreach and research program in agricultural economics, with a focus on the issues facing California’s farm economy. The appointee will bolster our applied research footprint across the state and help meet the needs of California's agricultural sector through applied research on agricultural production costs and returns, farm-level costs and impacts of regulation, and of management strategies that strengthen profitability and long-run economic viability. The successful candidate is expected to oversee UC Davis ARE's world-renowned Cost and Return studies program (Cost and Return Studies). Other courses that the appointee may be asked to teach include MS level courses in agricultural economics and finance (ARE 223, ARE 271), and PhD level courses in empirical methods (ARE 202B, ARE 202C), and agricultural economics (ARE 231, ARE 232, and ARE 233). Position description The Chair serves as the strategic, academic, and administrative leader of the Department of Family and Community Medicine, responsible for advancing its clinical, educational, research, and community missions. Working closely with School of Medicine, the health system, and FQHC leadership, the Chair will expand the clinical enterprise, strengthen key partnerships, and foster a collaborative and supportive environment for faculty, staff, learners, and residents. The Chair will promote interdisciplinary research, enhance the Department's nationally recognized residency program, and develop future leaders in primary care and health services research. With an appreciation for the matrixed nature of UC Davis, the Chair will integrate research, education, clinical care, and community engagement while ensuring the Department remains a thriving academic practice. This is an exceptional opportunity for a visionary and collaborative leader to shape the future of family medicine and advance the health of the communities served by UC Davis. The successful Chair for the Department of Family and Community Medicine candidate will: Develop and execute a clear strategic vision aligned with the priorities of the School of Medicine and UC Davis Health. Serve as a visible and influential advocate for the Department within the institution, the community, and nationally. Expand and integrate high-quality clinical services across the care continuum. Recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty, staff, and trainees while fostering a culture of engagement and professional growth. Advance the Department's research enterprise through mentorship, collaboration, and scholarly excellence. Ensure clinical quality, accountability, and continuous performance improvement across all providers. Maintain excellence in undergraduate, graduate, and continuing medical education programs. Strengthen partnerships across UC Davis Health, the School of Medicine, and the community to advance shared clinical, educational, and research goals. Provide strong financial stewardship to ensure the Department's long-term growth and sustainability. The candidate must be eligible to hold an appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level. As a faculty member, responsibilities include clinical service in the area of specialty, as applicable; teaching medical students and post-graduate trainees; conducting bench/clinical/translational research leading to peer-reviewed publication; and University service. All responsibilities will be further determined based on faculty series. For the full position description and to apply, visit recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07779. Position description The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invites applications and nominations for a nationally and internationally recognized academic obstetrician-gynecologist to join the faculty of the David Geffen School of Medicine (DGSOM) as the Chair of the Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology (OB/GYN). Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Health Sciences, the Dean of the DGSOM, and the President and CEO of the UCLA Health System via Executive Medical Director, the Chair works collaboratively with clinical, academic, and administrative leaders to establish and execute the strategic vision of the Department of OB/GYN within the greater health system. The Chair is responsible for advancing the Department’s mission of excellence in clinical care, education, research, and community engagement through the development of educational programs, research and innovation; oversight of clinical operations, financial management, staffing, performance improvement, faculty recruitment, and strengthening community partnerships. In addition, the Chair cultivates a collegial, inclusive, and multidisciplinary culture consistent with the principles of the DGSOM’s Cultural North Star, providing mentorship to faculty members, while also upholding UCLA Health’s patient-experience model, CICARE, and promoting clinical quality, safety, and operational distinction. Home to nationally recognized programs spanning the full spectrum of women’s health, the Department of OB/GYN is a leader in clinical innovation, scientific discovery, and academic excellence. The Department includes seven clinical divisions, with more than 120 faculty members across a broad network of clinical partners and affiliated programs, including Harbor-UCLA, Olive View Medical Center, Cedars-Sinai, Kern Medical, West Los Angeles VA Medical Center, Kaiser Permanente, and Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science. With anticipated clinical expansion in the years ahead, the Department is poised for continued growth in the reach and impact of its programs. This expansive academic and clinical network creates a rich environment for collaboration and discovery by integrating the Department’s clinical divisions with expertise across genetics, physiology, molecular, cellular and developmental biology, pediatrics, and other interdepartmental disciplines. With robust residency, fellowship, and medical student programs, the Department plays a vital role in training future leaders in women’s healthcare and research. This role offers an exceptional opportunity to build upon UCLA’s longstanding tradition of excellence and to further elevate the Department’s national and international influence. The ideal candidate is a distinguished obstetrician-gynecologist with outstanding accomplishments in leadership, clinical care, research, education and service, as well as a passion for interdepartmental collaboration and growth in a complex and evolving environment. Course / Program Description General Chemistry for Life Scientists CHEM XL 14A General Chemistry for Life Scientists I This course provides an introduction to physical and general chemistry and is geared towards pre-medical and pre-health students. This course is the first course in the general and organic chemistry series. CHEM XL 14B General Chemistry for Life Scientists II This course is the conclusion of general chemistry and introduces organic chemistry. This course is geared towards pre-medical and pre-health students and is the second course in the general and organic chemistry series. Structure of Organic Molecules CHEM XL 14C Structure of Organic Molecules This course is a continuation of organic chemistry in the organic chemistry series. This course is geared towards pre-medical and pre-health students and is the fourth and final course in the general and organic chemistry series. Job Description The Department of Public Health and Sustainability at UCLA Extension offers a wide variety of certificate programs and courses including transfer-credit (XL) and post-baccalaureate credit-bearing (X-400 level). All courses are offered using the Canvas Learning Management System (LMS). Applications to teach are accepted throughout the year in order to fill immediate program needs and to increase the depth of the instructor pool. Position description The Center for Neuroscience (CNS) in the College of Biological Sciences and the Department of Neurology in the School of Medicine at the University of California, Davis invite applications for a position in fundamental neuroscience. We seek an outstanding candidate using cutting-edge approaches to understand the mechanisms of brain function and dysfunction at the molecular, synaptic, circuit or cognitive levels. Candidates should value the opportunity to work in close collaboration with both research and clinical faculty. A Ph.D. or M.D. or equivalent and postdoctoral experience in an appropriate discipline are required. The successful applicant will be expected to have an active research program, a strong commitment to high quality teaching, the potential to attract extramural funding, and excellent potential for interactions/collaborations with existing faculty at the CNS and in the Neurology department. The applicant’s accomplishments in innovative research and commitments to teaching should demonstrate their potential to develop into the future leaders of their fields. The successful applicant will hold an academic appointment in the School of Medicine, Department of Neurology and will contribute to the undergraduate teaching mission of the University as well as to the University-wide Neuroscience Graduate Program. They will be housed in the Center for Neuroscience, an interdisciplinary research center that is home to more than 20 laboratories working collaboratively in all areas of neuroscience. The neuroscience community at UC Davis is broad and well-integrated across campus school and colleges, with exceptionally close and collegial interactions among between members of the Center and faculty from other neuroscience-focused institutes, departments, and graduate programs. Required materials include a cover letter (1-page summarizing interest in this position, including how their research would complement existing programs at CNS), updated curriculum vitae, statement of research accomplishments and future plans (max 3 pages), and a statement of teaching experience and philosophy (1 page), authorization to release information form, and 3-5 supporting letters of reference. All materials must be received by December 1, 2026, to be assured consideration. The search will continue until the position is filled through June 30, 2027. Position description The Department of Psychiatry and Neurosciences, which is a rapidly growing department in the University of California, Riverside School of Medicine, is recruiting up to three tenure track or tenured faculty members at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. We seek highly accomplished scholars with active research programs focused on behavioral health equity and translational and clinical neurosciences research. The focus on equity and health justice may be combined with any number of substantive areas. We are especially interested in outstanding scholars whose research, teaching, and service on health equity are coupled with expertise in health services delivery, implementation science, community-based participatory research, behavioral health, substance use, environmental health, climate change, public health informatics, or structural and social determinants of health. Deep interest and commitment to conducting collaborative research with diverse populations of Inland Southern California is a preferred qualification. Candidates must possess a PhD, DrPH, EdD, MD, or equivalent degree in psychiatry, neurosciences or psychology or other related field applied to mental health research, such as public or population health, anthropology, economics, education, political science, preventive medicine, sociology, and quantitative methods. Candidates seeking a clinical appointment must possess an MD, PhD, or equivalent degree and be eligible to practice in the State of California. Physician candidates must be board certified or board eligible. Applicants interested in a clinical appointment must qualify for medical staff privileges at UCR Health and our affiliated hospitals. The School of Medicine at UCR is the sixth University of California medical school and serves the rapidly growing, diverse, and dynamic Inland Southern California region by training a much-needed physician and biomedical workforce and catalyzing innovations in research, education, and health care delivery that will improve the health of medically underserved populations. The School of Medicine, Department of Psychiatry and Neuroscience is home to Community Responsive and Engaged Equity Research (CREER) in Mental Health, a center for research, education, and community leadership led by Dr. Lisa Fortuna in addition to Center for Health Disparities Research (CHDR), which is funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The successful candidate(s) will have opportunities to collaborate with researchers in CREER and CHDR. In addition, the School of Medicine is home to the Center for Healthy Communities (CHC), which serves the needs of Inland Southern California’s culturally, linguistically, and economically diverse communities. Position description We invite applications for the position of Director of the Center for Mind and Brain (Center for Mind and Brain), at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor (with tenure) in the Department of Psychology at the University of California, Davis. The Center for Mind and Brain (CMB) is an interdisciplinary research facility comprising faculty from multiple disciplines within the College of Letters and Science, College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, College of Biological Sciences and School of Medicine. For nearly 25 years, the CMB has been a nationally and internationally recognized leader in research on the human mind and brain. Combining strengths in cognitive and developmental psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, neurology, computational modeling and more, the 21 core faculty investigate the full arc of human mind and brain science across the lifespan to understand how minds develop, adapt, and thrive, while supporting and training undergraduate students, graduate students and postdoctoral scholars in leading-edge research. The Department of Psychology (Psychology) includes 41 faculty conducting research and teaching in 5 core areas, including cognition, perception and cognitive neuroscience; developmental psychology; biological psychology; quantitative psychology; and social and personality psychology. Our collaborative, interdisciplinary culture fosters innovation and supports high-impact scholarship. The successful candidate for Director will be expected to assume a high-profile leadership role to support and advance the research and training excellence of the CMB. The Director will hold a 50% administrative appointment for an initial 5-year period, with potential for renewal. The Director will be expected to implement a vision for expanding the CMB’s mission as a world-renowned research hub, to promote the individual and collaborative research programs of the CMB faculty, to identify and lead new opportunities for growth, and to strengthen the CMB’s ties to the many affiliated units at UC Davis, as well as international sites. The Director’s own research program could be in any area that is complementary to the mission of the CMB and the Department of Psychology. To be considered, applicants must have a PhD degree, an excellent record of accomplishment in scholarly research and teaching, and demonstrated leadership and administrative experience. Demonstrated success in obtaining federal and philanthropic extramural funds is expected. The start date for this position is July 1, 2027. Applications must be submitted by 11:59pm (PT) on Sunday October 11, 2026 for full consideration. Applications submitted after this date may not be considered. If you have any questions about the search or position, feel free to contact the Search Committee Chair, Dr. Joy Geng (jgeng@ucdavis.edu). This position offers the opportunity to work with a heterogeneous patient population and contribute to UCSF’s mission to improve healthcare quality and access for all patients. Position description The UCSF Division of Palliative Medicine (DPM), based at our UCSF Health sites, is seeking applications for full-time or part-time faculty. Our goal is to create opportunities for faculty to achieve academic success and a rewarding career in academic palliative medicine through clinical experiences that match their interests and opportunities for clinical innovation and program development, teaching, educational scholarship, research, quality improvement, and more. Highlights of this role include: • Outstanding and dedicated colleagues, staff, and trainees of all levels (e.g. medical students, residents, fellows) and of multiple disciplines • Academic environment with commitment to excellence and innovation in patient care, education, and research • Strong interdisciplinary teams where each member is highly valued as an equal contributor • Culture of support, mentorship, and leadership development • Diverse practice settings, including inpatient palliative care services at multiple sites, outpatient clinics, video telemedicine, and a home-based program • A cutting-edge research environment within the DPM and across UCSF, which affords virtually unlimited opportunities for research and other types of academic productivity • Dedicated time for scholarly work and opportunities for leadership of clinical, educational, and research programs • An institutional culture that is collaborative and highly receptive to palliative care • Patient populations from a range of backgrounds and communities in a beautiful, vibrant city Candidates may be at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level; rank and series will be commensurate with qualifications. Position description The University of California, Davis, School of Medicine, Department of Emergency Medicine is recruiting 3-4 full-time faculty members at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank in the Health Sciences Clinical Professor (HSCP) series or the Clinical X (Clin X) series. These positions offer an exceptional opportunity to join a nationally recognized department committed to excellence in clinical care, education, research, and community engagement UC Davis Emergency Medicine provides comprehensive emergency services to a large urban and referral population as a Level One Trauma Center, paramedic base station, and regional training center. The department has a fully accredited residency training program, established in 1990, that now includes 60 residents, as well as 11 fellowship programs spanning a wide range of subspecialties. All faculty members contribute meaningfully to both bedside and didactic teaching for residents, medical students, and rotating trainees. The department consistently ranks among the top 20 nationally in NIH funding and is a member of the federally funded SIREN (adult) and PECARN (pediatric) emergency care research networks. Faculty benefit from a robust research infrastructure and an academic environment that prioritizes discovery, innovation, and the implementation of new knowledge into clinical practice. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to clinical excellence, scholarship, and education. Responsibilities include providing outstanding clinical care, engaging in teaching and mentoring at multiple levels of training, and contributing to the academic mission of the department through research or educational innovation, depending on series. Candidates should also demonstrate dedication to mentoring a diverse student body, expanding opportunities, and enhancing academic success and retention. Position description The College of Biological Sciences at the University of California, Davis invites applications and nominations for a 9-month, tenure-track position in the Department of Evolution and Ecology at the ASSISTANT PROFESSOR level. The Department of Evolution and Ecology is seeking a plant evolutionary biologist with interests in the evolution of plants at any taxonomic, geographic, organizational, or evolutionary scale. Candidates must have a Ph.D. (or equivalent) in the biological sciences, evolutionary biology, ecology, genetics, or a related field, and will be expected to complement and build upon existing faculty strengths in the Department of Evolution and Ecology and across UC Davis. We welcome applicants working on any group of plants and using empirical, computational, experimental, and/or theoretical approaches. Possible areas of study are broad, and include macroevolutionary research on plant diversification, trait evolution in a phylogenetic context, major evolutionary innovations, comparative genomics, and evolutionary developmental biology, as well as research focusing at or below the species level including population biology, quantitative genetics, adaptive evolution, speciation, biogeography, and the evolution of life histories or species interactions. The Department of Evolution and Ecology is home to a collaborative and internationally recognized community of evolutionary biologists and ecologists, with close ties to the Center for Population Biology, the UC Davis Genome Center, and the graduate groups in Population Biology, Integrative Genetics and Genomics, and Ecology. The successful candidate will join a vibrant intellectual community with exceptional opportunities for collaboration across departments, colleges, and organized research units at UC Davis. Most notably, UC Davis is also home to a world-renowned cadre of plant biologists across campus departments and units, including the Departments of Plant Biology, Plant Sciences, Plant Pathology, Environmental Science and Policy, and Molecular and Cellular Biology, and the graduate groups in Plant Biology, Horticulture and Agronomy, Ecology, and Integrative Genetics and Genomics. These campus-level strengths in plant biology will position the new faculty member to collaborate across departments and colleges while reinforcing our department’s central role in the study of evolution. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong, extramurally funded, independent research program, teach effectively in undergraduate and graduate programs, and mentor a diverse community of undergraduate and graduate students. Depending on expertise, this faculty member could contribute to teaching in the introductory biology series (BIO 1, 2, or 3), upper-division courses in evolution (EVE 100) or genetics (BIS 101), and could teach existing or develop new upper-division courses in plant evolution or organismal biology. We seek a colleague committed to fostering an inclusive and collegial environment consistent with the UC Davis Principles of Community. Position description The University of California, Santa Barbara announces a strategic expansion of its world-leading quantum research enterprise, building on an unrivaled legacy of excellence recently punctuated by the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics. This initiative reinforces an extraordinary community of faculty whose work spans the full quantum spectrum—from superconducting qubits and synthetic materials to the theoretical foundations of quantum topology. UCSB leverages a premier research infrastructure including the NSF Quantum Foundry, the Eddleman Quantum Institute, and a state-of-the-art Nanofabrication Facility. These resources, combined with deep on-campus partnerships with global technology giants, position the university at the forefront of the federal government's "big bets" in quantum information science. To further strengthen this elite group, recruitment is underway for three foundational faculty positions in the first phase of this strategic cluster hire: an Atomic, Molecular, and Optical (AMO) Experimentalist in Physics, JPF03135; a specialist in Quantum Topology in Mathematics ; and an Experimental Physical Chemist in Chemistry and Biochemistry, JPF03152 Faculty Position: Quantum Topology & Quantum Computing As a vital part of this Quantum Cluster, the Department of Mathematics at the University of California, Santa Barbara invites applications for a tenure track faculty position at the level of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. The Department is looking for accomplished mathematicians with a particular emphasis in the area of QuantumTopology broadly construed, and its intersections with quantum computing. Preference will be given to candidates with strong potential to collaborate with researchers in other disciplines, especially physics or computer science, as well as to interact robustly with colleagues specializing in Topology. Responsibilities of faculty members generally include the development of an actively funded research program of high quality, teaching at undergraduate and/or graduate levels, mentorship of undergraduate students, recruitment, supervision, and mentorship of graduate students, and participation in university service and professional activities that meets expectations for faculty rank and step. UCSB has a strong tradition of collaborative research, and successful candidates will be able to leverage synergies across the campus as appropriate to their field. Our Research Environment UC Santa Barbara offers a unique environment where innovative, interdisciplinary, and foundational research is conducted in a collegial atmosphere. We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated exceptional promise through novel research. Position description Faculty Position Institute for Human Genetics University of California, San Francisco The UCSF Institute for Human Genetics invites applications for multiple faculty positions at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level in the ladder rank or in-residence series. Applicants with varied backgrounds in genetics and genomics will be considered, including those with expertise and interest in disease diagnosis and therapeutics, functional genomics, statistical genetics, and human population genetics. Candidates are expected to have demonstrated significant research accomplishment and potential, foster equity and inclusion in human genetics, and be committed to the mentorship of learners. The UCSF Institute for Human Genetics serves as a focal point for campus-wide activities in human genetics and has outstanding faculty members engaged in human genetics research spanning the four schools: Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and Dentistry. jobs.description: Application Window Open date: August 28, 2026 Next review date: Sunday, Sep 27, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee. Position description Faculty Positions – Master of Science in Regulatory Science and Digital Innovation (RSDI) Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences School of Pharmacy University of California, San Francisco The Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences (BTS) at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) invites applications for full-time faculty positions in the Adjunct Professor series at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank. These positions will support the newly established Master of Science in Regulatory Science and Digital Innovation (RSDI), an innovative graduate program launching in Summer 2027. The program is designed to prepare future leaders in regulatory science, digital health, artificial intelligence, medical product development, and global regulatory strategy through two academically equivalent pathways: a full-time Foundational Track and a hybrid Executive Track. The RSDI program was developed in collaboration with FDA scientists, industry leaders, and UCSF faculty and represents a major institutional investment in the future of regulatory science education. We seek candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Product Development, Entrepreneurship, and Leadership Digital Regulatory Science, including AI/ML-enabled medical products, Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), digital health, regulatory informatics, and real-world evidence Global Regulatory Strategy and Quality Systems, including multinational regulatory submissions, international harmonization frameworks, the WHO prequalification program, and quality management systems. Successful candidates will contribute to graduate education through course leadership, curriculum development, academic advising, and program service. Faculty members will serve as course directors, supervise capstone projects and master's theses, participate in admissions and curriculum committees, and collaborate with academic, industry, healthcare, and regulatory partners. One faculty member will also serve as Associate Director of the program with broader leadership responsibilities within the RSDI program. In addition to teaching responsibilities, the faculty member will engage in research and scholarship in regulatory science, broadly defined, encompassing areas such as toxicology, clinical pharmacology, small-molecule and biologic therapeutics, novel modalities, medical devices, diagnostics, and digital health. Research employing computational, quantitative, data-driven, or other approaches that do not require dedicated laboratory space is particularly encouraged. Candidates must possess a doctoral degree (e.g. PhD, PharmD, MD, DrPH, ScD) or equivalent terminal degree (e.g. JD, MBA) in a relevant discipline. Applicants should demonstrate expertise in one or more of the areas designated above, as well as evidence of excellence or strong potential for excellence in graduate-level teaching and student mentorship. Preferred qualifications include experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, diagnostics, or digital health sectors; experience working with or collaborating with regulatory agencies; experience in graduate or executive education; and demonstrated leadership in academic, industry, governmental, or professional settings. The selected candidate(s) will be appointed in the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences within the UCSF School of Pharmacy. Position description The Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging at the University of California, San Francisco invites candidates to apply for the position of Faculty Radiochemist. The selected candidate will be appointed at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in the In Residence or Adjunct series depending on qualifications and interests. The candidate will work collaboratively with faculty within the Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging and other departments at UCSF to advance the development of new molecular imaging agents, from early tracer development to first-in-man clinical studies. The successful candidate will establish and maintain a nationally recognized, externally funded research program, mentor students and postdoctoral researchers, and participate in departmental, university, and professional service activities. Required qualifications (to be met by the time of the faculty appointment start date) include: Ph.D. in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline. At least two years postdoctoral or equivalent research experience. Has demonstrated success in securing external research funding as principal investigator and/or in collaboration. Evidence of expertise in radiochemistry and related experimental methodologies. Strong written and oral communication skills. Commitment to excellence in teaching, mentorship, and collaborative research. Preferred qualifications include: Expertise in nuclear chemistry, targeted radionuclide therapy, radiopharmaceutical production, and regulatory oversight of radiopharmaceuticals in human subjects. Experience working with multiple radionuclides, including radiometals and radiohalogens, for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Experience in the development and radiolabeling of small molecules for diagnostic and/or therapeutic applications. Experience in the development and radiolabeling of biologics for diagnostic and/or therapeutic applications. Experience with radiopharmaceutical production workflows. Experience with regulatory submissions for first-in-human radiopharmaceutical work (IRB, FDA IND applications). Experience working with radiation safety programs and regulatory compliance. Record of interdisciplinary collaboration. Commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive academic environment. jobs.description: Position overview Position title: Assistant Professor of Narrative Film and Media Production Salary range: Commensurate with qualifications and experience; academic year (nine-month basis). A reasonable estimate for this position is $100,000 to $125,000. Anticipated start: July 1, 2027, with the academic year beginning in September 2027. Degree requirements must be met by June 30, 2027, for employment effective July 1, 2027 and beyond. Final date: Wednesday, Jun 30, 2027 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled. Position description The Department of Film & Digital Media at the University of California, Santa Cruz (UCSC) invites applications for the tenure-track position Assistant Professor of Narrative Film and Media Production. We are seeking applicants whose innovative creative work demonstrates an active and sustained practice in narrative form, expansively defined, with expertise in moving image media, production, and exhibition. Building on the department’s well-established strengths in documentary film and media, social justice-centered approaches to creative practice, and work that critically and creatively engages emerging technologies, we are particularly interested in candidates whose work bridges narrative and documentary practices, engages community-based and collaborative methods, or explores evolving modes and technologies of production. We welcome candidates whose work engages in a broader range of media practices, including interactive, participatory, and immersive media. The position will require the assistant professor to maintain an active creative research practice with a record of exhibition in festival, theatrical, streaming, or broadcast contexts. Our campus follows a schedule of three 11-week quarters per academic year. According to the department's workload policy, faculty members are expected to deliver the equivalent of four five-unit courses each year. The successful candidate will teach core and advanced camera-based production classes and foundational production workflows, including screenwriting, working with actors, cinematography, editing, and sound design across our three academic programs: undergraduate, M.F.A. in Social Documentation, and critical practice Ph.D. The primary curricular need for this position is in narrative-oriented camera-based workflows, including preproduction, production, and postproduction. While the modalities of research and creative practice are open, the candidate must be able to support core areas of the production curriculum. Our department values interdisciplinary scholarship and practice, and we are interested in candidates who can further expand the skillsets and modalities that we can offer our students. Further responsibilities of the position encompass advising and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, engaging in faculty governance at both departmental and campus levels, and actively partaking in administrative service for the department, the affiliated college, and the university as a whole. UC Santa Cruz is a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI) with a high proportion of first-generation and low-income students. We welcome candidates who understand the historical barriers that exist in higher education and who can clearly articulate how their teaching, mentoring, creative/professional activity, and service contribute towards building a just scholarly community. Position description Academic General Gastroenterology Physician Scientist Ladder Rank/In Residence Professor The Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, at the University of California, Davis School of Medicine is recruiting for 1 full-time faculty member in the Ladder Rank/In Residence series at the Professor rank in Gastroenterology. Faculty in the Ladder Rank/In Residence series are expected to engage in professional competence and activity, teaching, research and creative work, and University/public service. EXPECTATIONS The position will be primarily dedicated to establishing and maintaining an extramurally funded research program in cell therapies for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The final candidate will be expected to provide gastroenterology consultation and endoscopy services focused on patients with IBD at ambulatory sites located in the greater Sacramento region and share in call at the UC Davis Medical Center. Educational responsibilities will include supervision of consultations and procedures by fellows, residents, and medical students as well as providing lectures to various audiences. The GI Division currently includes 27 faculty and 4 nurse practitioners, who provide services at 5 clinics and 5 ambulatory endoscopy units, with ongoing expansion. Strengths of the division include robust programs in motility, IBD, advanced endoscopy and a new liver transplant program. Clinical research within the division is supported by the GI Clinical Research Unit which includes 8 research coordinators and staff supporting over 50 studies. The division has a long-standing history of providing outstanding patient care and medical education and recent expansion on the training program to include 12 GI Fellows and 1 Advanced Endoscopy Fellow. UC Davis Health serves a 65,000-square-mile area that includes 33 counties and 6 million residents across Northern and Central California. The UC Davis Medical Center is a 600-plus bed hospital with further expansion ongoing including an innovation hub, Aggie Square, and the 14-story California Tower. For the full position description and to apply, visit (https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07823). Faculty will participate in the education and training of Doctor of Nursing Practice students. The selected candidate will be appointed at the level of Assistant, Associate, or Full rank in the Health Sciences (HS) Clinical series depending on their qualifications and experience. Position description The Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging at the University of California, San Francisco invites candidates to apply for the position of Imaging Scientist Faculty in Molecular Imaging and Theranostics. The selected candidate will be appointed at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in the In Residence or Adjunct series depending on qualifications and interests. The new faculty member is expected to develop an independent research program in molecular imaging. We seek an innovative scholar with expertise in preclinical molecular imaging, nuclear chemistry, radiolabeled biologics, peptides or small molecules, and theranostics. The candidate will work collaboratively with faculty within the Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging and other departments at UCSF to advance the development of new molecular imaging agents, from early tracer development to first-in-man clinical studies. The successful candidate will establish and maintain a nationally recognized, externally funded research program, mentor students and postdoctoral researchers, and participate in departmental, university, and professional service activities. Required qualifications (to be met by the time of the faculty appointment start date) include: Ph.D. in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biology, Cancer Research or a closely related discipline. At least two years postdoctoral or equivalent research experience. Has demonstrated success in securing external research funding. Evidence of expertise in preclinical molecular imaging, theranostics, or nuclear chemistry. Strong written and oral communication skills. Commitment to excellence in teaching, mentorship, and collaborative research. Preferred qualifications include: Experience with computational methods applied to molecular engineering or radiopharmaceutical development. Experience in the development and radiolabeling of radiopharmaceuticals for diagnostic and therapeutic applications using a variety of medically relevant radionuclides. Experience with regulatory submissions for first-in-human radiopharmaceutical work (IRB, FDA IND applications). Experience working with radiation safety programs and regulatory compliance. Record of interdisciplinary collaboration. Specific areas of expertise with regards to disease focus are flexible and could include neurological, oncology, cardiology, or other clinical applications. The successful candidate will work with basic scientists and clinical researchers in planning, conducting, and evaluating data. The candidate is also expected to work closely with other departments at UCSF including the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology. Faculty are required to teach residents, fellows, medical students, and master’s students. The total compensation for this position ranges from $200,000-$320,000. Position description Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology Description: The Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology seeks to recruit faculty at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level. Candidates must have a strong background in immunology, genomics, genetics, genome engineering, synthetic biology and/or clinical immunotherapy, and significant achievements and meaningful promise in their field. We invite applications from scientists with Ph.D., M.D. (or equivalent degree), or M.D/Ph.D. degrees (or equivalent degrees) who are establishing or have established a research program in genomic immunology research. Relevant areas of research include, but are not limited to: Functional genomic studies in cells of the immune system Genome engineering to enhance adoptive cellular therapies Genetic/genomic studies of human diseases of the immune system Protein design and engineering in the context of the immune system and immunotherapies Systems immunology and immunotherapy Disease expertise in autoimmunity, inflammation or other conditions that may benefit from future immunotherapies Investigators will be expected to develop extramurally sponsored research programs and educate, mentor, and develop graduate and medical students. Successful candidate(s) will be appointed to an appropriate UCSF department as an Assistant, Associate or Full Professor (in residence or ladder-rank), and will be assigned dedicated research space on the UCSF Parnassus Campus and/or at Gladstone Institutes at Mission Bay. About Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology To harness the immense potential offered by immunotherapies, the Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology combines emerging biomedical technologies at the intersection of human immunology, genomics, CRISPR genome engineering, computational biology, and synthetic biology. The institute’s scientists deepen knowledge of how DNA sequences control cell functions in the human immune system. Their discoveries will enable the next generation of immunotherapies for cancer, autoimmune diseases, infectious diseases, inflammation and beyond. This institute is the result of a close partnership between Gladstone Institutes and the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). With wet and dry lab space to be housed (starting in 2027) in a new building on the Mission Bay campus, it creates a unified community across the two campuses and combines UCSF’s world-class immunology and planned cell therapy efforts with Gladstone’s expertise in the host-pathogen interface, iPS cells, computational biology, and CRISPR gene editing technologies. About Gladstone Institutes Gladstone Institutes is an independent, not-for-profit research organization affiliated with the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) and a renowned center of excellence focused on applying basic science to disease. Our science contributes to the health and wellbeing of all people through research, education, and outreach in the areas of cardiovascular disease, neurological disease, virology, immunology, and data science. Gladstone has a vibrant group of labs and core facilities focused on emerging and highly innovative technologies for biomedical research, including stem cells, imaging, single-cell genomics, mass spectrometry, and genome editing. Bioinformatics and biostatistics play a central role in this collaborative team.
